newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain IndMin plans to liberalise gas immediately.
newsitem.headline: Spain IndMin plans to liberalise gas immediately.

text.p: Spain's Industry Ministry plans to liberalise the gas market immediately, once the bill to reform the electricity market has been presented to parliament and regardless of expected moves by the European Commission.

Adressing a seminar on Monday, Energy Secretary Nemesio Fernandez Cuesta said: "The elements of the European directive on gas are sufficiently well-known that we can go ahead with opening the Spanish market.
"We want to go ahead with the liberalisation of gas as soon as possible."
Fernandez Cuesta said the new gas regulations would change the current negotiated access by third parties to a specifically structured access.
"Everyone who fulfils the "qualified" client conditions will have rights to access, and tariffs will be established by the government" he said.
Under the new rules, initial requirements to access the gas network will likely be that the interested party will be an electricity generator consuming more than 25 million cubic metres.
He said this would mean the Spanish market is 39 percent deregulated, versus a 30 percent level established by the European Commission for the first stage.
The new system would abolish the tariff being set according to usage type as at present, which would mean that industrial tariffs will fall.
Fernandez Cuesta said: "The specific industrial tariff will become a general tariff, and the difference between the two will be around 30 percent."
The new regime will look at different formulas which may also be applicable to rates charged, such as the distance transported, take or pay agreements and the structure of supply.
